title: Once ‘capital of the Confederacy’, Virginia enshrines rights to voting, abortion and gay marriage

blocks.text:
Organizers won key civil liberties protections on election day – and women and Black advocates were at the forefront

Progressives made historic gains in the south during the midterm elections – and Virginia was no exception. The state approved three constitutional amendments protecting civil liberties that have eroded in Trump’s second term: enshrining the rights to abortion and same-sex marriage, and restoring voting rights to those with past felony convictions.

These victories were led by women and Black organizers who say they want to capitalize on the momentum and advocate for policies that expand the protections they secured on election day.
